title: Impact of self-association on the architectural properties of bacterial nucleoid proteins
one_liner_zh: 该文通过粗粒化模型和布朗动力学模拟研究细菌核仁蛋白自聚集对DNA构象组织的影响，属于广义蛋白质-DNA互作建模，方法可迁移至TF-DNA体系，但对象非典型TF-DNA。
abstract: The chromosomal DNA of bacteria is folded into a compact body called the nucleoid, which is composed essentially of DNA (80%), RNA (10%), and a number of different proteins (10%). These nucleoid proteins act as regulators of gene expression and influence the organization of the nucleoid by bridging, bending, or wrapping the DNA. These so-called architectural properties of nucleoid proteins are still poorly understood. For example, the reason why certain proteins compact the DNA coil in certain environments but make instead the DNA more rigid in other environments is the matter of ongoing debates. Here, we address the question of the impact of the self-association of nucleoid proteins on their architectural properties and try to determine whether differences in self-association are sufficient to induce large changes in the organization of the DNA coil. More specifically, we developed two coarse-grained models of proteins, which interact identically with the DNA but self-associate differently by forming either clusters or filaments in the absence of the DNA. We showed through Brownian dynamics simulations that self-association of the proteins increases dramatically their ability to shape the DNA coil. Moreover, we observed that cluster-forming proteins compact significantly the DNA coil (similar to the DNA-bridging mode of H-NS proteins), whereas filament-forming proteins increase instead significantly the stiffness of the DNA chain (similar to the DNA-stiffening mode of H-NS proteins). This work consequently suggests that the knowledge of the DNA-binding properties of the proteins is in itself not sufficient to understand their architectural properties. Rather, their self-association properties must also be investigated in detail, because they might actually drive the formation of different DNA/protein complexes.
abstract_zh: 细菌的染色体DNA折叠成一个称为拟核（nucleoid）的紧凑结构，其主要由DNA（80%）、RNA（10%）和多种不同蛋白质（10%）组成。这些拟核蛋白作为基因表达的调控因子，并通过桥接、弯曲或缠绕DNA来影响拟核的组织结构。这些所谓的拟核蛋白结构特性仍未被充分理解。例如，某些蛋白质在特定环境中压缩DNA线圈，而在其他环境中反而使DNA变得更刚性的原因，仍是当前争论的焦点。在此，我们探讨拟核蛋白自结合对其结构特性的影响问题，并试图确定自结合的差异是否足以诱导DNA线圈组织发生重大变化。更具体地，我们开发了两种粗粒化蛋白质模型，它们与DNA的相互作用相同，但在缺乏DNA时通过形成簇或丝状体而表现出不同的自结合方式。通过布朗动力学模拟，我们表明蛋白质的自结合显著增强了它们塑造DNA线圈的能力。此外，我们观察到形成簇的蛋白质显著压缩DNA线圈（类似于H-NS蛋白的DNA桥接模式），而形成丝状体的蛋白质则显著增加DNA链的刚性（类似于H-NS蛋白的DNA刚性化模式）。因此，这项工作表明，仅了解蛋白质的DNA结合特性不足以理解其结构特性；相反，还必须详细研究其自结合特性，因为它们可能实际驱动不同DNA/蛋白质复合物的形成。
